_comment: Ablation config for D-NeRF (no mask; readCamerasFromTransforms never sets a mask for Blender/D-NeRF data, ignore_mask=true kept for explicitness/consistency with configs_dnerf.json, same no-op as there). Parameter under test = sparse_anchor.anchor_stride (see 'ablation' below). Based directly on configs_dnerf.json with iterations LEFT AT 40000 (full baseline, not halved like configs_ablation.json did for nerf_ds) per explicit user request. anchor_stride itself is NOT read from this file at run time: full_ablation_dnerf.py overrides it per run via train.py's --anchor_stride CLI flag (CLI always wins over configs.json, see arguments/__init__.py's ParamGroup) -- the value here is only the fallback default if the script is ever invoked oddly. All other optimization/sparse_anchor settings (densify_until_iter=16000, densify_grad_threshold=0.0006, knn_k=48, coarse_levels=3, anchor_refine_iters, dyn_select_iter=9500) are UNCHANGED from configs_dnerf.json: unlike NeRF-DS, D-NeRF's fixed T=150 training frames keeps the anchor count M tiny (~38 at the heaviest anchor_stride=4, vs NeRF-DS's up to ~213) regardless of stride or freeze timing, so none of the memory-safety retuning that configs_nerf_ds_without_mask.json needed (after a real OOM on this same 20GB GPU) applies here -- see full_ablation_dnerf.py's docstring for the full time-budget derivation and the explicit caveat that this has NOT been benchmarked end-to-end yet.

ablation._comment: 4 values x 8 dnerf scenes = 32 runs. Smaller stride = more anchors (M) = slower/heavier; larger stride = fewer anchors = faster/lighter. Spans both sides of configs_dnerf.json's baseline default (4, the heaviest here since dnerf has no larger default to contrast against).
